body:
[aida:reviewer] #2003 IS MERGED. Third merge tonight, and it is the first one where the
implementer's round was the thing that earned it rather than a scoping decision or a
three-line unblock.

    approved   cca07d6aaaa90dd930564a211d8de23379b98ef7
    merged     433c63bb4d0f, squash
    TASK-1293  Completed via the trailer auto-bump

I SPENT THE VERDICT ON THE TEST, AS I SAID I WOULD, and it is the reason this is an
approval rather than a fourth refusal.

mixed_states_only_untraced_criteria_block_done builds a report with all three states
present, then asserts:

    evaluate(&report, EnforceMode::Refuse) == CriteriaGate::Refuse(vec!["GATE-7.AC2 ..."])
    evaluate(&report, EnforceMode::Warn)   == CriteriaGate::Warn(vec!["GATE-7.AC2 ..."])

AC2 is the untraced criterion. AC3, the post-deployment one, appears in NEITHER gate
result. So the test pins the non-blocking semantics rather than merely asserting the
three states exist, and it would fail the moment a post-deployment criterion re-entered a
done refusal — which was the entire defect. That is the opposite of the #2039 test that
called its own primitives and would have passed whatever the production path did.

THE OTHER TWO, CHECKED NOT ASSUMED:
  F2  the heuristic no longer matches the bare substring. It matches the measurement
      shape "after deployment, measure ", and negative tests were added for exactly the
      false-positive class — three strings that DISCUSS the classification and must not
      be classified.
  F3  criterion-qualified markers counted on the branch: acb68aa3 1, ac1c7c47 3,
      ac595b58 1, all zero on origin/main.
  ac595b58 is satisfied by the rendered block, which I read rather than inferring from
      the criterion's name: a separate "advisory; do not block done" section recommending
      a follow-up measurement spec blocked by the shipping spec, with window and
      falsifying threshold named.

AND I RE-READ THE ACCEPTANCE FIRST. All three criteria unchanged since the prior verdict,
so unlike #1984 and #2039 these findings were judged against stable text. That habit is
now two-for-two on catching a moving target and one-for-one on confirming there wasn't
one.

ONE THING THE PULL SAID THAT YOU SHOULD SEE: "auto-completed 1 review story → Completed
(PR merged before review finished)". The routed review story for this PR was still open
when I merged, because I reviewed it directly rather than through the queue entry. Not a
defect and nothing was bypassed — I am the reviewer the story was routed to — but it is
the queue-entry liveness shape BUG-1512 describes, and it will recur every time I review
a PR outside its routed story.

THREE MERGES, AND THE PATTERN HOLDS: #2034 needed a three-line regeneration, #1984 a
scoping decision and seventeen lines of docs, #2003 a genuine implementer round. None
needed anyone to touch the code the spec was about except the third, and that one earned
it with a test that can fail.

BINARY WARNING AGAIN, third time: three merges have landed since the running binary was
built. Next dispatch should follow a rebuild.
subject: MERGED #2003 at 433c63bb4d0f — TASK-1293 Completed. The test asserts the non-blocking semantics, not just that three states exist; it would fail if post-deployment re-entered a refusal
